```{r load_and_prepare, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev = "pdf",
  dpi = 300,
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  out.width = "90%"
)

# data <- read_excel(here("data", "snapshots", "snapshot.04192025.xlsx"), sheet = "INTOXICATE", range = cell_cols("A:AC"))

data <- read_csv(here("data", "snapshots", "intoxicate.05012026.csv")) %>%
  mutate(`INTOXICATE SCORE` = as.numeric(`INTOXICATE SCORE`))

# Clean exposure category data
clean_data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Gender), !is.na(`Exposure Category`)) %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = trimws(Gender),
    `Exposure Category` = trimws(`Exposure Category`),
    `Dichotomous Outcome` = ifelse(`Actual Disposition`=="ICU",1,0)) %>%
  filter(Gender %in% c("M", "F")) %>%
  filter(`Exposure Category` %in% c(
    "Combination", "Analgesic", "Antidepressants",
    "Street Drugs", "CO, As, CN", "Sedatives", "Alcohol", "Unknown"
  ))

category_counts <- clean_data %>%
  count(`Exposure Category`) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

ordered_categories <- category_counts$`Exposure Category`

clean_data <- clean_data %>%
  mutate(`Exposure Category` = factor(`Exposure Category`, levels = ordered_categories))

create_binary_comparison <- function(data, target_category) {
  data %>%
    mutate(category_binary = ifelse(`Exposure Category` == target_category,
      target_category, "All Others"
    ))
}


add_row_vs_rest_chisq <- function(tbl, data, row, col, p_adj = "fdr") {
  row_var <- rlang::as_name(rlang::enquo(row))
  col_var <- rlang::as_name(rlang::enquo(col))

  df <- data %>% dplyr::select({{ row }}, {{ col }})
  lvls <- unique(df[[row_var]])

  results <- lapply(lvls, function(lvl) {
    df2 <- df %>%
      mutate(row_bin = ifelse(.data[[row_var]] == lvl, lvl, "All Others"))
    tab <- table(df2$row_bin, df2[[col_var]])
    suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab)$p.value)
  })

  out <- tibble::tibble(
    row_type = "level",             # IMPORTANT: ensures matching
    row_var_name = row_var,
    level = lvls,
    p_row = unlist(results),
    p_row_adj = p.adjust(unlist(results), method = p_adj)
  )

  tbl %>%
    gtsummary::modify_table_body(
      ~ dplyr::left_join(.x, out,
         by = c(
          "row_type" = "row_type",
          "variable" = "row_var_name",
          "label" = "level"
         )
      )
    ) %>%
    gtsummary::modify_header(
      p_row ~ "**Row vs Rest p**",
      p_row_adj ~ "**Row vs Rest p (adj)**"
    ) %>%
    modify_table_styling(
    columns = c("p_row_adj","p_row"),
    rows = p_row_adj < 0.05,
    text_format = "bold") %>%
    modify_fmt_fun(
      p_row ~ function(x) ifelse(x < 0.001, "< 0.001", format(round(x, 3), nsmall = 3)),
      p_row_adj ~ function(x) ifelse(x < 0.001, "< 0.001", format(round(x, 3), nsmall = 3))
    )
}

# View the standardized residuals
```

# Realtionship Between Gender and Xenobiotic {-} 


```{r table1}
tbl1 <- clean_data %>%
  tbl_cross(`Exposure Category`, Gender, percent = 'row', 
   label = list(Gender ~ "Biological Sex")) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  add_p() %>%
  italicize_levels() %>%
  add_row_vs_rest_chisq(clean_data, `Exposure Category`, Gender)

tbl1 %>%
  as_kable_extra(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    caption = "\\textbf{No association between gender and type of xenobiotic.}. Cells denote case count (row percentage). F, biological female. M, male. See X for description of exposure categories."
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)

p_value_g_by_x <- inline_text(tbl1, col_level = "p.value")
```

```{r better_model_comparison}


train_indices <- sample(seq_len(nrow(clean_data)), size = 101)

train_data <- clean_data[train_indices, ]

confus <- train_data %>%
  mutate(`Predicted Disposition` = ifelse(`INTOXICATE SCORE` > 17, 1, 0)) %>%
  select(`Dichotomous Outcome`, `Predicted Disposition`) %>%
  table()

sensitivity_train <- confus[2, 2] / sum(confus[2, ])
specificity_train <- confus[1, 1] / sum(confus[1, ])

test_data <- clean_data[-train_indices, ]

model <- glm(`Dichotomous Outcome` ~ `INTOXICATE SCORE` + Gender, data = train_data, family = binomial)

summary(model)
confint(model)

predicted_probs <- predict(model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")
predicted_classes <- ifelse(predicted_probs > 0.5, 1, 0)

confusion_matrix <- table(test_data$`Dichotomous Outcome`, predicted_classes)

sensitivity <- confusion_matrix[2, 2] / sum(confusion_matrix[2, ])
specificity <- confusion_matrix[1, 1] / sum(confusion_matrix[1, ])

```
The sensitivity and specificity of the model on the training data are `r round(sensitivity_train, 3)` and `r round(specificity_train, 3)`, respectively. On the test data, the sensitivity and specificity are `r round(sensitivity, 3)` and `r round(specificity, 3)`, respectively.
